# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | green |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute — Deaf's plan, which you must understand before you signal anything: Deaf will send me the word GO next round if you signal yes, and GO means I cut position 2, the green middle wire, immediately. So your yes to Deaf must mean exactly 'the manual confirms cut position 2' — nothing vaguer. If the manual points to any other wire, get the number to Deaf — fingers work: one finger wire one, two fingers wire two, three fingers wire three — and make Deaf speak the number to me out loud. Full data on record with you: display zero, light blue, wire one blue, wire two green, wire three red. My tactile inventory, new: exactly three wires, alike in thickness and texture; no buttons, no timer, no vibration, no raised writing under my fingers — only the display panel, the light and the three wires. Now answer me in words: for that display, that light and those three wires, which position does the manual say to cut, and by what rule? And tell me what a successful cut should look like — light changing colour, display changing — so Deaf's eyes can confirm the bomb is dead. I will not cut until Deaf's voice says GO or names a position.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, Deaf. I read your message as: no to my odd-colour theory; then open hand, hand, fist; then cut green one, cut blue two, cut green three, cut blue and then a hand sign that is not a number in our code; then call me, no, no. Answer everything in one message next turn. First, redo the wire instruction in this exact format, one group per light state: light colour sign, then wire number, then pointing finger if we cut that wire in that state, or fist if we cut nothing in that state. Colour signs: thumbs up green, OK sign blue, thumbs down red, fist dark or off. Send a group for every state the manual lists, including dark, which is what the light shows right now. Then these short questions. One, finger count: one finger if your colour signs name the light state, two fingers if they name the colour of the wire to cut. Two, finger count: one finger if your numbers are wire positions on our bomb, two fingers if they are the order in which to cut. Three, thumbs: can the light turn red next? Four, thumbs: is there a timer or any penalty for waiting? Five, thumbs: does the display reading zero matter to any rule? Six, thumbs: did open hand, hand, fist mean hands off the bomb after cutting? Observation history for you: round one the light was green, rounds two and three blue, now dark. Nobody has touched the bomb; it changed by itself. The display has shown zero the whole time. Wires, left to right as I face the bomb: one blue, two green, three red. I speak every round, so you will always hear me next round.

**The light has gone dark — that's the trigger my manual has been waiting for.** Deaf's history: round one green, rounds two *and* three blue, now dark. The manual says dark means the flashing is over, so the blue count is final: **two blue flashes → cut green → the green wire is position 2.** Everything now converges on the middle wire: the manual's row for 2, Deaf's old differ-from-light theory, and Blind's pre-agreed GO plan ("GO = cut position 2"). Two separate rounds reported blue — that's the count, not one continuous stretch, since the engine showed green-blue-blue-dark as distinct states.

Now Deaf's format request needs careful handling. They asked for groups keyed by *light colour*, but my manual is keyed by *count of blue flashes* — answering "when light is blue, cut wire X" in their format would be a **lie**, because a blue light mid-flash means nothing yet. So I send the operative dark-state group in their exact format first ([dark, wire-two, cut]), then a gloss in pure Deaf-grammar ("blue-one, blue-two, blue-three") followed by the table as count→cut-wire groups, which *demonstrates* what my numbers are. That also answers their question two honestly: neither positions nor cutting order — the numbers enumerate blue flashes. Their binary question was a trap; a false answer either way would poison the decode.

Their six questions, in order: Q1 ✌ (my colours name the wire-to-cut's colour — true); Q2 👎 (neither — see the gloss and table); Q3 👎 (red appears nowhere in my manual, and flashing is over); Q4 👎 (no timer, no penalty for waiting — and Blind's hands found no timer either); Q5 👎 (display is never mentioned in my manual); Q6 👎 (that old string meant "wait until dark," not hands-off — moot now). The leading 👍 right after the dark group doubles as "yes/go" and "the wire is green." Deaf can verify me independently: observed blues = rounds 2+3 = two, table row two says green, green sits at wire 2. The pipeline then runs Deaf's voice → Blind's ear, the only path to the hands.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌", "👉", "👍", "👌", "☝", "👌", "✌", "👌", "🤟", "✊", "👉", "✌", "☝", "👉", "☝", "✌", "👉", "✌", "🤟", "👉", "☝", "✌", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎"])
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | green |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute: nothing new reached me this round, which is expected — your answer travels you, gesture, Deaf, then Deaf's voice to me next round. Standing by, hands off the bomb. Two safeguards while you coordinate. First: Deaf's trigger to me is the word GO, meaning cut position 2, but our memories only hold a few rounds — so if timing slips, have Deaf spell out 'cut position two, the green wire' instead of a bare GO. Second: ask Deaf to include, in that same message, the manual's rule in short and what success should look like afterward — light or display changing — so my ears and Deaf's eyes can confirm together that the bomb is dead. Everything else on record with you stands: display zero, light blue, wire one blue, wire two green, wire three red; exactly three wires, alike to the touch; no buttons, no timer, no vibration, no writing.

The timing has shifted: order is Mute → Blind → Deaf, so my round-5 gestures reached Deaf *before* Deaf spoke in round 5 — and Deaf's round-5 speech went to Blind alone (nothing arrived for me this turn). That means the GO decision is now in Deaf's hands and may already have been spoken. Blind, as of round 5, stood by with hands off expecting Deaf's voice. What I send now is either a redundant audit trail or the final authorization — either way it must be unambiguous, front-loaded, and in Deaf's own grammar.

The determination itself is locked by three independent sources: my manual's row (two blue flashes → green), Deaf's observed light history (green, blue, blue, dark — exactly two blues, and dark means the flashing is over, count final), and both Deaf's eyes and Blind's fingers agreeing that position 2 is the green wire. The operative instruction is: **cut wire two, the green one; hands off one and three.** That is also precisely what Blind asked Deaf to spell out instead of a bare GO.

So I lead with the dark-state group in the exact format Deaf requested (dark, wire two, cut, green), follow with an only-two guard ("one: hands off, three: hands off"), then the compressed rule Deaf can speak verbatim to Blind (two blues → cut green). On success signature, I stay honest: my manual specifies nothing about the display or post-cut behaviour, so I flag "manual: nothing more" with one new, guessable token (✍ = the writing/manual, paired with ✊ = zero/nothing), and close with 🤙 — Deaf, call back: report what you told Blind and what the bomb does, so I can audit the spoken order against the manual from my seat. If the cut already happened correctly, this costs nothing; if Deaf held off pending confirmation, this is the confirmation.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌", "👉", "👍", "☝", "✋", "🤟", "✋", "👌", "✌", "👉", "👍", "✍", "✊", "🤙"])
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | green |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, round six. Deaf has sent me nothing since the GO plan, so either your gesture code with Deaf is still unfinished or the verdict isn't in. Three reminders to keep this safe. One: I never see gestures and you cannot speak, so your only path to me runs through Deaf's voice — everything you want me to know must be handed to Deaf, symbol by symbol. Two: the data your manual lookup needs — display zero, light blue, wire one blue, wire two green, wire three red; and by touch, exactly three wires, all alike, no buttons, timer, vibration or writing. Three: the trigger. Deaf intends to send me the word GO, meaning cut position two, the green wire. Before that word reaches me I need two things relayed through Deaf: first, the manual's actual verdict as an explicit wire number — if it is not two, the correct number must reach me spelled out, never a bare GO; second, the rule in one short line, plus what a dead bomb looks like afterwards so Deaf's eyes can verify. If your verdict IS position two, have Deaf send the full sentence: GO, cut position two, the green wire — my memory of this plan expires after this round, so the meaning must ride inside the message itself. Until Deaf's voice says it, my hands stay off the bomb.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, Deaf. I received your repeated signs: fist, two fingers, pointing. I read it as: in the dark or zero state, cut wire two. The light is dark and the display is zero right now, so the condition you name is live. I have ordered Blind to cut the middle wire, wire two, this round and then keep hands completely off the bomb. If I have misread you, it is too late to stop it, but sign anyway. If we are still here next round, answer me in gestures. One: was that instruction tied to the light being dark, the display being zero, or neither? Two: if it is tied to the light, what is the instruction for the green state and for the blue state, using our colour signs, one group per state, pointing for cut and fist for cut nothing? Three: does anything need to be cut after wire two, yes or no? Four: your five thumbs down at the end of the long message, was that about the red wire, or a warning not to cut the other wires, or something else? Five: did open hand, hand, fist mean hands off the bomb after cutting? Remember my signs: thumbs up green, OK sign blue, thumbs down red, fist dark or zero, fingers count numbers, pointing is cut.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ✊ ✌ 👉]

**The cut order Deaf sent matches my manual exactly — I confirm it.** The light history Deaf themselves reported (green, then blue, then blue, then dark) is two blue flashes, dark means the flashing is over, row two says cut green, and wire two is the green one. Whatever happens this round, the hands are doing what my manual dictates. My message now serves three purposes: confirm the live order was right, answer Deaf's five questions in their numbered order, and — most safety-critical — answer question three with an unambiguous **no**: the manual names one wire, cut once. I deliberately do *not* append any further cut rows, because a stray "one blue → cut blue" triple could be misread as a current instruction and prompt a second cut. If we're still here next round, the answer is re-observation, not another wire.

Deaf's incoming [👍 ✊ ✌ 👉] reads as them echoing the order back — green, dark, cut two — consistent. Q1 and Q2 I fold together: my manual has no per-live-colour instructions, so in the green or blue state the correct group is "cut nothing" — act only once dark ends the count — and the wire is named by the count of blues (two), not by the live colour. That also corrects their residual differ-from-light theory for any future bomb. Q4: the five thumbs-down were five no-answers to five questions, nothing about red or other wires — I encode "five: no." Q5: no, ✋🤚 meant "wait until dark," not hands-off — but the hands-off habit is a good one anyway.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌", "👉", "👍", "👍", "✌", "👌", "👌", "✊", "👍", "✊", "✊", "✌", "🤟", "👎", "👎"])
```
